findings.title: Apache 2.4.49 is vulnerable to CVE-2021-41773 (path traversal / RCE)
findings.description: This exact Apache version is affected by CVE-2021-41773 / CVE-2021-42013: a path traversal flaw in mod_proxy that allows reading files outside the document root and, with mod_cgi enabled, remote code execution.
findings.impact: Unauthenticated remote code execution on the web server.
findings.remediation: Upgrade to Apache 2.4.51 or later immediately. As an interim mitigation, disable mod_cgi and require 'Require all denied' on the default filesystem path.

findings.title: CORS reflects any origin with credentials enabled
findings.description: http://127.0.0.1:8099/ returned Access-Control-Allow-Origin: https://sentwall-canary.example together with Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true. Any website on the internet can therefore make authenticated cross-origin requests and read the responses as the logged-in victim.
findings.impact: Complete account takeover from a single malicious link: the attacker reads profile data, API tokens and personal information, and can perform actions on the victim's behalf.
findings.remediation:
Never reflect the Origin header blindly. Use a strict allow-list:
if origin in TRUSTED_ORIGINS: set ACAO=origin, ACAC=true
else: do not send CORS headers at all.
Also reject the 'null' origin.

findings.title: Database dump exposed
findings.description: A SQL dump is downloadable. It contains full table data plus schema.
findings.impact: Mass disclosure of customer records, password hashes and business data - usually a reportable data breach.
findings.remediation: Delete the dump from the web root, store backups outside the document root or in object storage with signed URLs, and assess breach-notification obligations.
evidence: First lines: INSERT INTO users VALUES(1);

findings.title: Environment file with secrets exposed
findings.description: The .env file is downloadable. It normally contains database credentials, the application encryption key, mail passwords and third-party API keys.
findings.impact: Direct database access, ability to forge session cookies with the app key, and full compromise of every integrated service.
findings.remediation:
Deny access to dotfiles at the server, move the file above the web root, and rotate every credential it contains:
location ~ /\.(?!well-known) { deny all; }

findings.title: Exposed Git repository configuration
findings.description: The .git directory is publicly readable. An attacker can download the entire source history - including secrets that were committed and later 'removed' - and then reconstruct the full application source.
findings.impact: Complete source code disclosure, plus every credential, API key and database password that ever appeared in a commit. This typically leads to full server compromise.

findings.title: Path traversal / local file inclusion in 'file'
findings.description: A relative path payload caused the server to return the contents of /etc/passwd. The parameter is used to build a filesystem path without validation or confinement to a base directory.
findings.impact: Read of arbitrary server files - configuration, private keys, database credentials - and often escalation to remote code execution by including a file the attacker can upload.
findings.remediation:
Never pass user input to file APIs. Resolve the path and verify it stays inside the allowed directory:
real = os.path.realpath(os.path.join(BASE, name))
if not real.startswith(BASE + os.sep): abort(400)
Better: map an opaque ID to a stored path instead of accepting names.

findings.title: SQL injection in parameter 'q' (MySQL)
findings.description: Appending a single quote to 'q' produced a raw MySQL database error that does not appear on the normal page. The value is being concatenated directly into a SQL statement instead of being sent as a bound parameter.
findings.impact: Full database read and write: customer records, password hashes, payment data and admin credentials. Depending on database privileges this often escalates to remote code execution on the server. This is a reportable data-breach risk.
findings.remediation:
Use parameterised queries / prepared statements everywhere. Never build SQL by string concatenation.
PHP: $stmt = $pdo->prepare('SELECT * FROM t WHERE id = ?');
Java: PreparedStatement with setInt/setString
Also apply least-privilege DB accounts and disable detailed DB errors in production.
evidence: Database error signature: you have an error in your sql syntax

findings.title: Server-side template injection in 'name'
findings.description: A template expression was evaluated server-side: the payload {{7658*417}} was rendered as 3193386. User input is being compiled as template code.
findings.impact: Depending on the template engine this escalates to arbitrary command execution on the server - typically full infrastructure compromise.
findings.remediation: Never render user input as a template. Pass it as a variable, and use logic-less templates or sandboxed rendering.

findings.title: Content-Security-Policy header is missing
findings.description: Without a CSP the browser will execute any script that reaches the page. This is the single most effective defence-in-depth control against cross-site scripting (XSS), malicious third-party scripts and data injection.
findings.impact: Raises the likelihood and blast radius of any injection flaw on the site; an attacker who lands one script gets a durable foothold in users' browsers.
findings.remediation:
Publish a restrictive CSP, starting in report-only mode:
Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self'
evidence: Response headers did not include: content-security-policy

findings.title: Cookies missing the Secure flag: PHPSESSID
findings.description: These cookies can be sent over plain HTTP. A single unencrypted request - a mistyped URL, an http:// link, a shared network - exposes them to anyone listening on the wire.
findings.impact: Session hijacking: an attacker who captures the cookie becomes the user without needing any password.
findings.remediation:
Set the Secure attribute on every cookie:
Set-Cookie: session=...; Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax; Path=/

findings.title: Could not establish a TLS connection on port 443
findings.description: No TLS handshake could be completed with the server on port 443. Either the site is HTTP-only, or the TLS stack is misconfigured.
findings.impact: All traffic - including logins and payment data - travels unencrypted.
findings.remediation: Install a valid certificate (Let's Encrypt is free) and serve the site exclusively over HTTPS.
evidence: Error: [WinError 10061] No connection could be made because the target machine actively refused it

findings.title: End-of-life Apache 2.4.49 in production
findings.description: The server reports Apache 2.4.49. Apache httpd below 2.4.55 has multiple published CVEs. Once a branch is end-of-life it receives no security patches, so every newly discovered vulnerability in it stays exploitable forever.
findings.impact: Known vulnerabilities in the runtime can be exploited at leisure; attackers actively scan for these versions.
findings.remediation: Upgrade Apache to a currently supported release and put a patch cadence in place (monthly minimum, plus out-of-band for critical advisories). Test on staging first.

findings.title: Missing Anti-CSRF Protection on State-Changing Form
findings.description: A sensitive POST form at action 'http://127.0.0.1:8099/login' on page http://127.0.0.1:8099/ does not contain an anti-Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) token.
findings.description_bn: http://127.0.0.1:8099/ পেজের ফর্মে কোনো CSRF প্রটেকশন টোকেন নেই।
findings.impact: An attacker can host a malicious webpage that silently submits requests on behalf of authenticated users without their consent, potentially altering account details, emails, or settings.
findings.impact_bn: অন্য কোনো ক্ষতিকর ওয়েবসাইট থেকে ব্যবহারকারীর অজান্তেই প্রোফাইল আপডেট বা পাসওয়ার্ড পরিবর্তন করে ফেলা সম্ভব।
findings.remediation: Implement unpredictable, cryptographically strong anti-CSRF synchronizer tokens for all state-changing POST/PUT/DELETE requests. Additionally, configure session cookies with `SameSite=Lax` or `SameSite=Strict`.

fix_patches.code:
<!-- Include CSRF Token in Form -->
<form method="POST" action="/account/update">
  <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token }}">
  <!-- inputs -->
</form>

findings.description: A sensitive POST form at action 'http://127.0.0.1:8099/admin/' on page http://127.0.0.1:8099/admin/ does not contain an anti-Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF) token.

findings.title: Reflected XSS in parameter 'name'
findings.description: User input supplied in 'name' is written back into the HTML page without encoding. The probe string was returned with its angle brackets intact, which means an attacker can inject any HTML tag - including <script> - and it will execute in the victim's browser.
findings.impact: Session theft, credential phishing rendered inside your own page, silent actions on behalf of the user, and malware delivery. Chained with a missing HttpOnly flag this is immediate account takeover.
findings.remediation:
Context-aware output encoding on every sink:
- HTML body: encode & < > " '
- attributes: quote and encode
- JavaScript/URL contexts: use the framework's escaper
Also validate input against an allow-list and add a strict CSP as defence in depth.

findings.title: Reflected XSS in parameter 'q'
findings.description: User input supplied in 'q' is written back into the HTML page without encoding. The probe string was returned with its angle brackets intact, which means an attacker can inject any HTML tag - including <script> - and it will execute in the victim's browser.
findings.impact: Session theft, credential phishing rendered inside your own page, silent actions on behalf of the user, and malware delivery. Chained with a missing HttpOnly flag this is immediate account takeover.
findings.remediation:
Context-aware output encoding on every sink:
- HTML body: encode & < > " '
- attributes: quote and encode
- JavaScript/URL contexts: use the framework's escaper
Also validate input against an allow-list and add a strict CSP as defence in depth.

findings.title: Reflected XSS through a form field
findings.description: Submitting a harmless HTML tag in this form's text field caused it to be rendered back unencoded.
findings.impact: Script execution in the context of the site whenever a crafted form submission is processed.
findings.remediation: Encode all user input on output and validate it on input.

findings.title: Cookies without SameSite attribute: PHPSESSID
findings.description: With no SameSite attribute, browsers fall back to their default behaviour and the cookie is attached to cross-site requests. That is exactly what a CSRF attack needs.
findings.impact: State-changing actions (password change, transfer, delete) can be triggered from an attacker's page while the victim is logged in.
findings.remediation: Add SameSite=Lax to normal session cookies; use SameSite=Strict for admin or high-value actions. Pair with anti-CSRF tokens.

findings.title: Directory listing is enabled
findings.description: The web server returns an auto-generated file index for http://127.0.0.1:8099/uploads/. Visitors can browse the contents of these folders directly, including files that were never meant to be linked.
findings.impact: Disclosure of uploaded documents, backups, temporary files and sometimes personal data belonging to other users.
findings.remediation:
Disable autoindex:
nginx: autoindex off;
Apache: Options -Indexes
and move non-public files outside the web root.

findings.title: HTTP TRACE method is enabled
findings.description: The server answers TRACE by echoing the full request back, including headers. Combined with a scripting flaw this enables Cross-Site Tracing (XST), which can read HttpOnly cookies.
findings.impact: Bypasses the HttpOnly protection on session cookies in some browsers.

findings.title: Open redirect via parameter 'url'
findings.description: The 'url' parameter controls where the user is sent, and it accepts any external host. The application will happily redirect visitors to an attacker-controlled site while the link still starts with your domain.
findings.impact: Highly effective phishing: 'https://yourdomain/login?next=evil.com' looks trustworthy, and is also used to steal OAuth tokens and bypass allow-lists.
findings.remediation: Accept only relative paths, or validate against an allow-list of permitted hosts before redirecting. Reject values containing '://' and '//'.

findings.title: Outdated jQuery 1.12.4 (known XSS issues)
findings.description: jQuery 1.12.4 predates fixes for CVE-2020-11022 / CVE-2020-11023 (XSS via htmlPrefilter) and, below 3.4.0, CVE-2019-11358 (prototype pollution in jQuery.extend).
findings.impact: Untrusted HTML passed to .html()/.append() can execute script, re-enabling XSS even where the application escapes correctly.
findings.remediation: Upgrade to jQuery 3.7.x and audit any .html() call that receives user data.

findings.title: Page can be framed by any site (clickjacking)
findings.description: Neither X-Frame-Options nor CSP frame-ancestors is set, so the site can be embedded in an invisible iframe on an attacker's page. Users can be tricked into clicking 'Delete account', 'Pay' or 'Grant access' while believing they are on a harmless page.
findings.impact: Account actions and payment flows can be hijacked through UI redressing.
findings.remediation: Add Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' (preferred) and X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN for older browsers.

findings.title: Session cookies readable from JavaScript: PHPSESSID
findings.description: Without HttpOnly, any JavaScript running on the page - including code injected through an XSS flaw or a compromised third-party script - can read the session cookie with document.cookie.
findings.impact: A single XSS anywhere on the site escalates from 'script execution' to full, persistent account takeover.
findings.remediation: Add HttpOnly to all session and authentication cookies.

findings.title: Absence of Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoint
findings.title_bn: অথেনটিকেশন এন্ডপয়েন্টে রেট লিমিটিং (Rate Limiting) এর অভাব
findings.description: The authentication endpoint at http://127.0.0.1:8099/login showed no evidence of rate limiting or brute-force throttling after rapid successive queries (no 429 status code or standard RateLimit-* headers detected).
findings.description_bn: http://127.0.0.1:8099/login এ কোনো রেট লিমিটিং নেই, ফলে হ্যাকাররা স্বয়ংক্রিয়ভাবে হাজার হাজার পাসওয়ার্ড ট্রাই করতে পারবে।
findings.impact: Allows malicious actors to perform automated credential stuffing, dictionary password attacks, or distributed brute-force attacks against user accounts without triggering throttling.
findings.impact_bn: সহজেই ব্রুট-ফোর্স (Brute-Force) বা ক্রেডেনশিয়াল স্টাফিং অ্যাটাক চালিয়ে ইউজারের অ্যাকাউন্ট হ্যাক করা সম্ভব।
findings.remediation: Enforce strict IP and account-based rate limiting on all login, registration, and password recovery endpoints. Return HTTP 429 (Too Many Requests) with a `Retry-After` header when thresholds are exceeded. Implement account lockouts or progressive CAPTCHA challenges after consecutive failed attempts.
evidence: Tested 6 rapid requests; all returned status 404
findings.poc_curl: for i in {1..10}; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' 'http://127.0.0.1:8099/login'; done

findings.title: Dangerous HTTP methods advertised: PUT
findings.description: The server advertises write-capable methods on a public endpoint. If the application layer does not authorise them, an attacker can upload or delete content directly.
findings.impact: Potential unauthorised file upload, overwrite or deletion.
findings.remediation: Restrict allowed methods to GET/POST/HEAD (plus OPTIONS if needed) and return 405 for the rest. Verify authorisation on every verb.
evidence: Allow: GET, POST, OPTIONS, TRACE, PUT

findings.title: External links open with target=_blank but no rel=noopener
findings.description: A link opened in a new tab keeps a reference to your page through window.opener. The destination site can use it to redirect the original tab to a phishing page.
findings.impact: Users who return to the original tab land on an attacker-controlled clone.
findings.remediation: Add rel="noopener noreferrer" to every target="_blank" link, or set it globally in the framework.

findings.title: HTML comments reveal internal information
findings.description: Developer comments are shipped to production. They often contain credentials, internal hostnames, TODO notes about unpatched areas, or hints about hidden admin paths.
findings.impact: Free reconnaissance for an attacker, sometimes including direct credentials.
findings.remediation: Strip comments in the build step (HTML minification does this automatically) and review what is deployed.
evidence: <!-- TODO: remove test admin:admin before launch -->

findings.title: Permissions-Policy header is missing
findings.description: Powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, clipboard) stay available to any embedded third-party frame unless explicitly disabled.
findings.impact: Raises the likelihood and blast radius of any injection flaw on the site; an attacker who lands one script gets a durable foothold in users' browsers.
findings.remediation:
Add a deny-by-default policy, e.g.:
Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), payment=()
evidence: Response headers did not include: permissions-policy

findings.title: Referrer-Policy header is missing
findings.description: Full URLs - including tokens and internal identifiers - leak to third parties through the Referer header when users click external links.
findings.impact: Raises the likelihood and blast radius of any injection flaw on the site; an attacker who lands one script gets a durable foothold in users' browsers.
findings.remediation:
Add:
Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin
evidence: Response headers did not include: referrer-policy

findings.title: Technology versions disclosed in response headers
findings.description: Response headers advertise the exact server and framework versions. An attacker can match these against public CVE databases and pick exploits that are known to work, skipping the reconnaissance phase entirely.
findings.impact: Faster, more reliable targeting of version-specific vulnerabilities.
findings.remediation: Suppress or genericise version strings: nginx `server_tokens off;`, Apache `ServerTokens Prod` / `ServerSignature Off`, PHP `expose_php = Off`, and remove X-Powered-By at the reverse proxy.

findings.title: Third-party scripts loaded without Subresource Integrity
findings.description: 1 script tag(s) load code from an external host without an integrity hash. If that CDN or vendor is compromised, the modified script runs with full access to your users' sessions.
findings.impact: One compromised third-party host becomes a compromise of your site.
findings.remediation:
Add integrity and crossorigin attributes:
<script src="https://cdn.example/lib.js" integrity="sha384-..." crossorigin="anonymous"></script>
findings.owasp: A08:2021 Software and Data Integrity Failures

findings.title: X-Content-Type-Options header is missing
findings.description: Browsers may 'sniff' a response into a different content type than declared, which can turn an uploaded file or user-controlled endpoint into executable script (MIME confusion attacks).
findings.impact: Raises the likelihood and blast radius of any injection flaw on the site; an attacker who lands one script gets a durable foothold in users' browsers.
findings.remediation:
Add to every response:
X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff
evidence: Response headers did not include: x-content-type-options

findings.title: Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy (COOP) header is missing
findings.description: COOP isolates your browsing context from cross-origin windows, closing cross-window attacks such as Spectre-style leaks and tabnabbing chains.
findings.impact: Raises the likelihood and blast radius of any injection flaw on the site; an attacker who lands one script gets a durable foothold in users' browsers.
findings.remediation:
Add:
Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin
evidence: Response headers did not include: cross-origin-opener-policy

findings.title: No web application firewall detected
findings.description: No WAF or CDN filtering layer was identified in front of the application. Nothing sits between the internet and the code to block obvious attack patterns.
findings.impact: Every malicious request reaches the application directly; there is no virtual patching option when a CVE drops.
findings.remediation: Consider a WAF/CDN (Cloudflare, AWS WAF, or a managed service). Treat it as defence in depth only - it never replaces fixing the underlying code.

findings.title: Password field allows browser autocomplete
findings.description: The login form does not set autocomplete="off" or a credential-manager hint. On shared devices this can leave credentials stored in the browser.
findings.impact: Minor credential exposure on shared computers.
findings.remediation: Use autocomplete="current-password" on login and "new-password" on registration so password managers behave correctly, and avoid autocomplete="off" on login (it breaks managers).

findings.title: robots.txt points at sensitive paths
findings.description: robots.txt lists directories that look sensitive. Bots ignore this file, and it is often the first thing an attacker reads - it works as a signpost rather than a control.
findings.impact: Guides attackers to admin, backup or internal paths.
findings.remediation: Do not rely on robots.txt for access control. Protect these paths with real authentication and remove the hints.
